rationale: Receipt 1a9292879a5642519ee6306b6376e255 finally exercises the target path: after the delayed Prepare and a Promise handled in Accept phase, node 5 applies an AcceptSync carrying the new leader's decided 4, its decided index drops from 5 to 4, read(4) changes from Decided(Value(5)) to Undecided(Value(5)), and it returns to 5 when the new leader re-decides. This update asserts the core visibility defect, promotes the executed observation, answers the three open gaps, and marks the question explained.

knowledge.statement: On the executed five-node run, node 5 had decided through index 5 and read index 4 as Decided(Value(5)); after the new leader's AcceptSync it reported decided 4 and read index 4 as Undecided(Value(5)); after the new leader re-decided index 5 it reported decided 5 and read index 4 as Decided(Value(5)) again. The same log index was therefore observed Decided, Undecided and Decided with unchanged value.
knowledge.conditions: Five OmniPaxos instances (pids 1..5), ClusterConfig {configuration_id:1, nodes:[1,2,3,4,5]}, MemoryStorage, batch_size 1, no snapshots. Entry 5 is accepted by 1,2,3,5 and decided by leader 1, but the Decide reaches only node 5; nodes 2 and 3 stay decided 4 with accepted 5. Node 1 is then cut, node 2 is elected with promises from 3 and 4 only (decided 4), and node 5's Prepare is delivered only after node 2 is in Accept, so its Promise is handled by handle_promise_accept and answered with an AcceptSync carrying decided 4.

knowledge.statement: A new leader's decided index is the maximum decided index among the promises that formed its prepare quorum (handle_majority_promises -> get_max_decided_idx). A follower whose Promise arrives after that quorum is answered by handle_promise_accept with send_accsync stamped with the leader's current decided index, and handle_acceptsync passes that value to sync_log, which assigns it to the decided index without comparing it to the follower's existing value. A follower that had already learned a later decision therefore loses decided progress until the new leader re-accepts and re-decides the entry.
knowledge.conditions: Majority quorum with five nodes; at least one member of the new leader's prepare quorum accepted the entry without deciding it; the more-informed follower is delayed past the quorum; no snapshots involved in the sync.

interpretations.rationale: The question is answered by a completed witness. Receipt 1a9292879a5642519ee6306b6376e255 ran late_promise_sync_regresses_decided (exit 0, test passed) and its single comparison (regressed eq true, applicability phase=after_sync) is complete and holds, evaluating event 1. Event 0 establishes the premise: leader 1 decided 5, node 2 decided 4 with accepted 5, and node 5 decided 5 with index 4 reading decided. Event 1 shows node 5 at decided 4 while its leader (node 2) is in Accept at decided 4, with entry_status undecided, regressed true, promise/acceptsync/accepted flags all true, node 5 in Accept and its promise at ballot n=2,pid=2; event 2 shows node 5 back at decided 5 with index 4 decided after the new leader re-decided. The mechanism is the one the source predicted: the new leader's decided index came from the promises it held when its prepare quorum formed (max 4), its AcceptSync to the late promiser carried that 4, and sync_log assigned it without comparing it to node 5's existing 5. Node 5 had already read index 4 as Decided, so the same entry changed status to Undecided and then back to Decided. That contradicts the documented guarantee that a decided entry is not reverted and is safe to apply (docs/omnipaxos/log.md), and an application applying Decided entries as it observes them can apply the same entry twice; a client polling get_decided_idx observes it going backwards. The decided value at the index is preserved and the new leader re-decides after its accept quorum acknowledges, so this is a decision-visibility and consumption defect, not a divergence of decided values, and the regression window is bounded by one accept round.

f48a2678152a46b987d08e37826d2ca5-gap-1.explanation: Yes. The corrected run shows promise_seen=true, acceptsync_seen=true and n5_accepted_reply=true; the AcceptSync carried node 2's decided index 4 (event 1: decided_leader2=4) and node 5 applied it, moving to Accept (n5_accept=true) and dropping to decided 4. The earlier absence was caused by the probe withholding that message.

9e2e871d737f4e6f829b8239c8cbc484-gap-2.explanation: Yes. After the Prepare was truly extracted from the queue, node 5 emitted a Promise, node 2 emitted an AcceptSync addressed to node 5, and node 5 emitted an Accepted reply, all observed in the corrected run.

423b10df284a4783b577202d1d0242ba-gap-3.explanation: Yes. With true extraction the leader emitted an AcceptSync to the late promiser carrying its lower decided index (4) and the follower applied it: decided fell from 5 to 4, read(4) became Undecided(Value(5)), and after re-decision both returned to 5/Decided.

counterevidence: If the delayed follower's Promise participates in the prepare quorum, its decided index enters the maximum and no regression occurs.
If every member of the prepare quorum had also received the earlier Decide, the leader's decided index already covers the entry and the sync lowers nothing.
The entry's value is never changed and the new leader re-decides the index, so this does not break agreement on values; it breaks the stability of the Decided status that applications rely on.
The three earlier runs of this probe were invalid constructions (delivered withheld messages, then re-queued them) and do not count as negative evidence.
limitations: One delayed promiser, majority quorum, unit batch size, memory storage and no snapshots; flexible quorums, batching and snapshot-based sync are unexercised.
The regression is observed at a synchronous sample immediately after the AcceptSync; its duration is the interval until the new leader re-decides, which this run measures only by the third event.
The probe drives leadership with try_become_leader and delivers messages explicitly; it does not exercise BLE election timing or a real network.
